original.target_description: Unassigned original side; not examined in this replication-only blind validation.

replication.target_description: Study 1: repeated-measures ANOVA main effect of emotion (crying, laughing, baseline talking) on summed person-oriented behaviours (looking, contacting, approaching, vocalizing), across owner/stranger conditions in domestic dogs tested at home. Located on article p. 238 (PDF p. 4).

n.sample_role: Dogs with complete behavioural coding for the repeated-measures behavioural analysis.
n.exclusions: 16 dog-owner pairs tested; one dog had behavioural data only for owner crying because of a camera malfunction. Heart-rate exclusions are separate from this behavioural test.
n.location: p. 238 (PDF p. 4), Data Analysis; total recruited sample p. 237, Participants
n.quote: Another dog only had behavioural data for the owner crying condition because of a camera malfunction. This left behavioural data for 14 dogs who had data in all heart rate conditions and 15 dogs with full data in behavioural coding.

es.location: p. 238 (PDF p. 4), Results, Behavioural Data, first paragraph; partial metric identified in Data Analysis on same page

p.location: p. 238 (PDF p. 4), Results, Behavioural Data, first paragraph (emotion main effect)

reported_success.quote: In this experiment, we replicated the Custance and Mayer (2012) study as expected.

notes: Published article supplied by licensed EBSCO PsycInfo service; supplied text title, authors and DOI match the assigned replication reference. Replication replaces humming with laughing. Effect size retained as printed; Data Analysis explicitly identifies effect-size measures as partial eta-squared. Printed F degrees of freedom (2, 15) retained without correction; the methods explicitly state 15 dogs with full behavioural coding, while other behavioural tests use denominator df 14 or 28. No sample size inferred from those degrees of freedom. Text extraction uses font glyphs ⫽, ⬍ and ␩2 in quoted statistics. Original side is an unassigned placeholder, not a finding that its source is unavailable.
